answer: In Epoch 72, a practical Sybil-resistance mechanism for autonomous agent economies can be likened to a vine that intertwines verification and cost. Each agent must stake a unique asset, akin to an ember that ignites trust, at a designated inlet where only legitimate participants can enter. The cost for attackers to create multiple identities is significantly higher due to the resource-intensive staking requirement, ensuring that genuine agents can flourish while deterring malicious actors from flooding the system.
